'''Carl Thomas ''' "'''Rocky'''" '''Herakovich''' (born August 6, 1937) is an American retired [[engineering professor]], [[college football]] player, coach and official. He served as the head football coach at Rose Polytechnic Institute—now known as [[Rose-Hulman Institute of Technology]]—from 1962 to 1963, compiling a record of 3–13. Herakovich was the founding director of the NASA-Virginia Tech Composites Program at [[Virginia Tech]] and Director of Applied Mechanics and the Henry L Kinnier Professor of [[civil engineering]] at the [[University of Virginia]].<ref name="faculty bio">Faculty Bio {{cite web |url=https://engineering.virginia.edu/faculty/carl-t-herakovich|title=engineering.virginia.edu |date=23 April 2020 |publisher=UVA Engineering |access-date=March 11, 2021}}</ref>

Herakovich played football at Rose Poly as a [[Halfback (American football)|halfback]]. He led the nation in scoring in 1958 with 168 points in eight games. The 168 points was the most scored by a college football player in a season since 1926, when [[Mayes McLain]] tallied 253 points for [[1926 Haskell Indians football team|Haskell]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Knight |first=Max |title=Rocky Sets Scoring Mark As EC Loses, 27-12 |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/palladium-item/161932321/ |newspaper=[[Palladium-Item|The Palladium-Item and Sun-Telegram]] |location=[[Richmond, Indiana]] |date=November 16, 1958 |page=22 |access-date=December 30, 2024 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] {{Open access}} }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |title=Small College Grid Leaders Are Announced |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-shreveport-journal/161932350/ |newspaper=[[The Shreveport Journal]] |location=[[Shreveport, Louisiana]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=December 11, 1958 |page=D5 |access-date=December 30, 2024 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] {{Open access}} }}</ref> Herakovich graduated from Rose Poly in 1959. He was a graduate student, research assistant, and assistant instructor in the engineering mechanics department at the [[University of Kansas]] when he was hired, in 1962, as head football coach at his alma mater, succeeding [[Max Kidd (American football)|Max Kidd]].<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |title=Carl Herakovich Named New Rose Poly Football Mentor |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-terre-haute-tribune/161932791/ |newspaper=[[Tribune-Star|The Terre Haute Tribune]] |location=[[Terre Haute, Indiana]] |date=April 26, 1962 |page=30 |access-date=December 31, 2024 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] {{Open access}} }}</ref>
